/**

 * @brief Devicetree main header
 *
 * API for accessing the current application's devicetree macros.
 */

#ifndef ZEPHYR_INCLUDE_DEVICETREE_H_
#define ZEPHYR_INCLUDE_DEVICETREE_H_

#include <zephyr/devicetree_generated.h>

#if !defined(_LINKER) && !defined(_ASMLANGUAGE)
#include <stdint.h>
#endif

#include <zephyr/sys/util.h>

/**
 * @brief devicetree.h API
 * @defgroup devicetree Devicetree
 * @since 2.2
 * @version 1.0.0
 * @{
 */

/*
 * Property suffixes
 * -----------------
 *
 * Do not put anything into the "Property suffixes" section below that does not
 * start with _dt_prop_ or DT_! This section is parsed during the build to
 * determine the set of valid property suffixes.
 */
/* begin: Property suffixes */
#define _dt_prop_prefix _P_
#define _dt_prop_suf_exists _EXISTS
#define _dt_prop_suf_ foreach _FOREACH_PROP_ELEM
#define _dt_prop_suf_foreach_sep _FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_SEP
#define _dt_prop_suf_foreach_vararg _FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_VARGS
#define _dt_prop_suf_ foreach_sep_vararg _FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_SEP_VARGS
#define _dt_prop_suf_len _LEN
#define _dt_prop_suf_idx_0 _IDX_0
#define _dt_prop_suf_idx_0_exists _IDX_0_EXISTS
#define _dt_prop_suf_idx_0_ph _IDX_0_PH
#define _dt_prop_suf_idx_0_val _IDX_0_VAL
#define _dt_prop_suf_idx_0_s_p _IDX_0_S_P
#define _dt_prop_suf_string_unquoted _STRING_UNQUOTED
#define _dt_prop_suf_string_token _STRING_TOKEN
#define _dt_prop_suf_string_upper_token _STRING_UPPER_TOKEN
#define _dt_prop_suf_enum_idx _ENUM_IDX
#define _dt_prop_suf_enum_val _ENUM_VAL
#define _dt_prop_suf_enum_token _ENUM_TOKEN
#define _dt_prop_suf_enum_upper_token _ENUM_UPPER_TOKEN
/* end: Property suffixes */

/**
 * @defgroup devicetree-generic-id Node identifiers and helpers
 * @ingroup devicetree
 * @{
 */

/**
 * @brief Invalid node identifier
 *
 * This can be used as a placeholder in generic code which needs an
 * expression that evaluates to a non-existent node identifier.
 *
 * Notice that if you pass this to another devicetree macro, you may
 * get thrust into a world of confusing C preprocessor error messages.
 * Check whether a node identifier exists before using it with
 * DT_NODE_EXISTS() if you are unsure.
 */
#define DT_INVALID_NODE _

/**
 * @brief Node identifier for the root node in the devicetree
 */
#define DT_ROOT DT_N

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for a devicetree path
 *
 * @note This macro returns a node identifier from path components.
 *       To get a path string from a node identifier, use
 *       DT_NODE_PATH() instead.
 *
 * The arguments to this macro are the names of non-root nodes in the
 * tree required to reach the desired node, starting from the root.
 * Non-alphanumeric characters in each name must be converted to
 * underscores to form valid C tokens, and letters must be lowercased.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     / {
 *             soc {
 *                     serial1: serial@40001000 {
 *                             status = "okay";
 *                             current-speed = <115200>;
 *                             ...
 *                     };
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * You can use `DT_PATH(soc, serial_40001000)` to get a node identifier
 * for the `serial@40001000` node. Node labels like `serial1` cannot be
 * used as DT_PATH() arguments; use DT_NODELABEL() for those instead.
 *
 * Example usage with DT_PROP() to get the `current-speed` property:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_PROP(DT_PATH(soc, serial_40001000), current_speed) // 115200
 * @endcode
 *
 * (Notice how `current-speed` in the DTS becomes `current_speed`
 * when used with C macros.)
 *
 * When determining arguments to DT_PATH():
 *
 * - the first argument corresponds to a child node of the root (`soc` above)
 * - a second argument corresponds to a child of the first argument
 *   (`serial_40001000` above, from the node name `serial@40001000`
 *   after lowercasing and changing `@` to `_`)
 * - and so on for deeper nodes in the desired node's path
 *
 * @param ... lowercase-and-underscores node names along the node's path,
 *            with each name given as a separate argument
 * @return node identifier for the node with that path
 */
#define DT_PATH(...) DT_PATH_INTERNAL(__VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for a node label
 *
 * Convert non-alphanumeric characters in the node label to
 * underscores to form valid C tokens, and lowercase all letters.
 * Note that node labels are not the same thing as label properties.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     serial1: serial@40001000 {
 *             label = "UART_0";
 *             status = "okay";
 *             current-speed = <115200>;
 *             ...
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * The only node label in this example is `serial1`.
 *
 * The string `"UART_0"` is *not* a node label; it's the value of a
 * property named `label`.
 *
 * You can use `DT_NODELABEL(serial1)` to get a node identifier for the
 * `serial@40001000` node. Example usage with DT_PROP() to get the
 * current-speed property:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_PROP(DT_NODELABEL(serial1), current_speed) // 115200
 * @endcode
 *
 * Another example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     cpu@0 {
 *             L2_0: l2-cache {
 *                     cache-level = <2>;
 *                     ...
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage to get the cache-level property:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_PROP(DT_NODELABEL(l2_0), cache_level) // 2
 * @endcode
 *
 * Notice how `L2_0` in the DTS is lowercased to `l2_0` in C.
 *
 * @param label lowercase-and-underscores node label name
 * @return node identifier for the node with that label
 */
#define DT_NODELABEL(label) DT_CAT(DT_N_NODELABEL_, label)

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier from `/aliases`
 *
 * This macro's argument is the name of a property of the `/aliases`
 * node. It returns a node identifier for the node which is aliased.
 * Convert non-alphanumeric characters in the alias property to
 * underscores to form valid C tokens, and lowercase all letters.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     / {
 *             aliases {
 *                     my-serial = &serial1;
 *             };
 *
 *             soc {
 *                     serial1: serial@40001000 {
 *                             status = "okay";
 *                             current-speed = <115200>;
 *                             ...
 *                     };
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * You can use `DT_ALIAS(my_serial)` to get a node identifier for the
 * `serial@40001000` node. Notice how `my-serial` in the devicetree
 * becomes `my_serial` in C. Example usage with DT_PROP() to get the
 * current-speed property:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_PROP(DT_ALIAS(my_serial), current_speed) // 115200
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param alias lowercase-and-underscores alias property name
 * @return node identifier for the node with that alias
 */
#define DT_ALIAS(alias) DT_CAT(DT_N_ALIAS_, alias)

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for an instance of a compatible
 *
 * All nodes with a particular `compatible` property value are assigned
 * instance numbers, which are zero-indexed integers Specific to that
 * `compatible`. You can get a node identifier for these nodes by
 * passing their instance numbers to this macro, along with the
 * lowercase-and-underscores version of the `compatible`.
 *
 * Instance numbers have the following properties:
 *
 * - For each compatible, instance numbers start at 0 and are contiguous.
 * - Exactly one instance number is assigned for each node with a
 *   compatible, **including disabled nodes**.
 * - Enabled nodes (status `"okay"` or not present) are assigned
 *   instance numbers before disabled nodes, and in no particular
 *   order among themselves.
 * - Disabled nodes (any other status) are assigned instance numbers
 *   after all enabled nodes, and again in no particular order among
 *   themselves.
 *
 * Notice that if a node has multiple strings in its `compatible`
 * property, it will have instance numbers for each of them,
 * generated independently with the above rules.
 *
 * Wait: before using this macro, check whether the file you are editing
 * has defined `DT_DRV_COMPAT` to the compatible you are interested in.
 * If so, check if you can use DT_DRV_INST() instead, as that makes
 * code portable to other compatibles.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     serial1: serial@40001000 {
 *             compatible = "vnd,soc-serial";
 *             status = "disabled";
 *             current-speed = <9600>;
 *             ...
 *     };
 *
 *     serial2: serial@40002000 {
 *             compatible = "vnd,soc-serial";
 *             status = "okay";
 *             current-speed = <57600>;
 *             ...
 *     };
 *
 *     serial3: serial@40003000 {
 *             compatible = "vnd,soc-serial";
 *             current-speed = <115200>;
 *             ...
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 *Assuming no other nodes in the devicetree have compatible
 * `"vnd,soc-serial"`, that compatible is assigned instance numbers
 * 0, 1, and 2 according to the above rules:
 *
 * - The nodes `serial@40002000` and `serial@40003000` are both enabled, so
 *   their instance numbers are 0 and 1, but which node gets which number is
 *   not guaranteed.
 * - `serial@40001000` is the only disabled node, so it has instance
 *   number 2, since disabled nodes are assigned numbers after enabled
 *   nodes.
 *
 * Therefore:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     // Could be 57600 or 115200. There is no way to be sure which:
 *     // either serial2 or serial3 could have instance number 0,
 *     // so this could be the current-speed property of either node.
 *     DT_PROP(DT_INST(0, vnd_soc_serial), current_speed)
 *
 *     // Could also be 57600 or 115200, for the same reason.
 *     // If the above expression expands to 57600, then this
 *     // expands to 115200, and vice-versa.
 *     DT_PROP(DT_INST(1, vnd_soc_serial), current_speed)
 *
 *     // 9600, because there is only one disabled node, and
 *     // disabled nodes are"at the end" of the instance
 *     // number list.
 *     DT_PROP(DT_INST(2, vnd_soc_serial), current_speed)
 * @endcode
 *
 * Notice how `"vnd,soc-serial"` in the DT becomes `vnd_soc_serial`
 * (without quotes) in the DT_INST()调用: the comma is replaced with
 * an underscore, and the hyphen is as well.
 *
 * @param inst instance number for compatible `compat`
 * @param compat lowercase-and-underscores compatible, without quotes
 * @return node identifier for the instance with that number and
 *         compatible
 */
#define DT_INST(inst, compat) UTIL_CAT(DT_N_INST, DT_DASH(inst, compat))

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for a parent node
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     parent: parent-node {
 *             child: child-node {
 *                     ...
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * The following produces the same node identifier:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_PARENT(DT_NODELABEL(child))
 *     DT_NODELABEL(parent)
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return a node identifier for the node's parent
 */
#define DT_PARENT(node_id) UTIL_CAT(node_id, _PARENT)

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for a grandparent node
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     gparent: grandparent-node {
 *             parent: parent-node {
 *                     child: child-node {
 *                             ...
 *                     };
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * The following produce the same node identifier:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_GPARENT(DT_NODELABEL(child))
 *     DT_PARENT(DT_PARENT(DT_NODELABEL(child))
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return a node identifier for the node's parent's parent
 */
#define DT_GPARENT(node_id) DT_PARENT(DT_PARENT(node_id))

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for a child node
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     / {
 *             soc-label: soc {
 *                     serial1: serial@40001000 {
 *                             status = "okay";
 *                             current-speed = <115200>;
 *                             ...
 *                     };
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage with DT_PROP() to get the status of the
 * `serial@40001000` node:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     #define SOC_NODE DT_NODELABEL(soc_label)
 *     DT_PROP(DT_CHILD(SOC_NODE, serial_40001000), current_speed) // 115200
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param child lowercase-and-underscores child node name
 * @return node identifier for the child node
 */
#define DT_CHILD(node_id, child) UTIL_CAT(node_id, DT_S_PREFIX(child))

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for a status `"okay"` node with a compatible
 *
 * Use this if you want to get an arbitrary enabled node with a given
 * compatible, and you do not care which one you get if there are
 * multiple matching nodes.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     node-a {
 *             compatible = "vnd,device";
 *             status = "okay";
 *     };
 *
 *     node-b {
 *             compatible = "vnd,device";
 *             status = "okay";
 *     };
 *
 *     node-c {
 *             compatible = "vnd,device";
 *             status = "disabled";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_COMPAT_GET_ANY_STATUS_OKAY(vnd_device)
 * @endcode
 *
 * This expands to a node identifier for either `node-a` or `node-b`.
 * It will not expand to a node identifier for `node-c`, because that
 * node does not have status `"okay"`.
 *
 * If there are no non-disabled nodes with `compatible`, this macro
 * expands to #DT_INVALID_NODE.
 *
 * @param compat lowercase-and-underscores compatible, without quotes
 * @return node identifier for an arbitrary node with that compatible,
 *         and status `"okay"`, or #DT_INVALID_NODE
 */
#define DT_COMPAT_GET_ANY_STATUS_OKAY(compat) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS_OKAY(compat), \
		    (DT_INST(0, compat)), (DT_INVALID_NODE))

/**
 * @brief Get a devicetree node's full path as a string literal
 *
 * This returns the path to a node from a node identifier. To get a
 * node identifier from path components instead, use DT_PATH().
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     / {
 *             soc {
 *                     node: my-node@12345678 {};
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *    DT_NODE_PATH(DT_NODELABEL(node)) // "/soc/my-node@12345678"
 *    DT_NODE_PATH(DT_PATH(soc))       // "/soc"
 *    DT_NODE_PATH(DT_ROOT)            // "/"
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return the node's full path in the devicetree
 */
#define DT_NODE_PATH(node_id) DT_CAT(node_id, _PATH)

/**
 * @brief Get a devicetree node's name with unit-address as a string literal
 *
 * This returns the node name and unit-address from a node identifier.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     / {
 *             soc {
 *                     node: my-node@12345678 {};
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *    DT_NODE_FULL_NAME(DT_NODELABEL(node)) // "my-node@12345678"
 *    DT_NODE_FULL_NAME(DT_PATH(soc))       // "soc"
 *    DT_NODE_FULL_NAME(DT_ROOT)            // "/"
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return the node's name with unit-address as a string in the devicetree
 */
#define DT_NODE_FULL_NAME(node_id) DT_CAT(node_id, _FULL_NAME)

/**
 * @brief Get a devicetree node's name with unit-address as a token
 *
 * This returns the node name and unit-address from a node identifier,
 * with non-alphanumeric characters converted to underscores.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     / {
 *             soc {
 *                     node: my-node@12345678 {};
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *    DT_NODE_FULL_NAME_TOKEN(DT_NODELABEL(node)) // my_node_12345678
 *    DT_NODE_FULL_NAME_TOKEN(DT_PATH(soc))       // soc
 *    DT_NODE_FULL_NAME_TOKEN(DT_ROOT)            // EMPTY
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return the node's name with unit-address as a token
 */
#define DT_NODE_FULL_NAME_TOKEN(node_id) DT_CAT(node_id, _FULL_NAME_TOKEN)

/**
 * @brief Get a devicetree node's name with unit-address as an uppercase token
 *
 * This returns the node name and unit-address from a node identifier,
 * with letters converted to uppercase and non-alphanumeric characters
 * converted to underscores.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     / {
 *             soc {
 *                     node: my-node@12345678 {};
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *    DT_NODE_FULL_NAME_UPPER_TOKEN(DT_NODELABEL(node)) // MY_NODE_12345678
 *    DT_NODE_FULL_NAME_UPPER_TOKEN(DT_PATH(soc))       // SOC
 *    DT_NODE_FULL_NAME_UPPER_TOKEN(DT_ROOT)            // EMPTY
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return the node's name with unit-address as an uppercase token
 */
#define DT_NODE_FULL_NAME_UPPER_TOKEN(node_id) DT_CAT(node_id, _FULL_NAME_UPPER_TOKEN)

/**
 * @brief Get a devicetree node's index into its parent's list of children
 *
 * Indexes are zero-based.
 *
 * Note that the index goes by the order of child nodes in the final
 * devicetree (after any overlays are applied), and includes disabled
 * child nodes as well.
 *
 * It is an error to use this macro with the #DT_ROOT node.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     parent {
 *             c1: child-1 {};
 *             c2: child-2 {};
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_NODE_CHILD_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(c1)) // 0
 *     DT_NODE_CHILD_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(c2)) // 1
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return the node's index in its parent node's list of children
 */
#define DT_NODE_CHILD_IDX(node_id) DT_CAT(node_id, _CHILD_IDX)

/**
 * @brief Do `node_id1` and `node_id2` refer to the same node?
 *
 * Both `node_id1` and `node_id2` must be node identifiers for nodes
 * that exist in the devicetree (if unsure, you can check with
 * DT_NODE_EXISTS()).
 *
 * The expansion evaluates to 0 or 1, and may be used in `#if`
 * conditionals.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     / {
 *             soc {
 *                     node_label: node@deadbeef {
 *                              status = "okay";
 *                     };
 *             };
 *
 *             aliases {
 *                     node-alias = &node_label;
 *             };
 *     };
 *
 *     other_node: other-node {};
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_SAME_NODE(DT_PATH(soc, node_deadbeef), DT_NODELABEL(node_label)) // 1
 *     DT_SAME_NODE(DT_ALIAS(node_alias), DT_NODELABEL(node_label))        // 1
 *     DT_SAME_NODE(DT_ALIAS(node_alias), DT_NODELABEL(other_node))        // 0
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id1 first node identifier
 * @param node_id2 second node identifier
 * @return 1 if the node identifiers refer to the same node, 0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_SAME_NODE(node_id1, node_id2) \
	(DT_DEP_ORD(node_id1) == (DT_DEP_ORD(node_id2)))

/**
 * @brief Get a devicetree node's status as a token, or `okay` if none
 *
 * This converts the node's status property to a lowercase token, or
 * evaluates to `okay` if the node has no status property.
 * Non-alphanumeric characters are converted to underscores.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return the status property as a token, or `okay`
 */
#define DT_STATUS(node_id) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_NODE_HAS_PROP(node_id, status), \
		    (DT_STRING_TOKEN(node_id, status)), (okay))

/**
 * @brief Get a devicetree node's status as an uppercase token, or `OKAY` if none
 *
 * This converts the node's status property to an uppercase token, or
 * evaluates to `OKAY` if the node has no status property.
 * Non-alphanumeric characters are converted to underscores.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return the status property as an uppercase token, or `OKAY`
 */
#define DT_STATUS_UPPER(node_id) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_NODE_HAS_PROP(node_id, status), \
		    (DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN(node_id, status)), (OKAY))

/** @} */

/**
 * @defgroup devicetree-generic-prop Property accessors
 * @ingroup devicetree
 * @{
 */

/**
 * @brief Get a devicetree property value
 *
 * For properties whose bindings have the following types, this macro
 * expands to:
 *
 * - string: a string literal
 * - boolean: `0` if the property is false, or `1` if it is true
 * - int: the property's value as an integer literal
 * - array, uint8-array, string-array: an initializer expression in braces,
 *   whose elements are integer or string literals (like `{0, 1, 2}`,
 *   `{"hello", "world"}`, etc.)
 * - phandle: a node identifier for the node with that phandle
 *
 * A property's type is usually defined by its binding. Within some
 * special nodes, like `/chosen`, binding types are not available, and
 * the type is inferred from the DTS value layout instead.
 *
 * For other properties or more specialized access to the above types,
 * see the documentation for the following macros:
 *
 * - DT_PHA() et al. for phandle-array and phandles properties
 * - DT_PHANDLE() et al. for phandle and phandles properties
 * - DT_STRING_TOKEN() and DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN() for string properties
 * - DT_PROP_BY_IDX() for array, string-array, uint8-array, and
 *   phandles properties
 * - DT_PROP_LEN() for getting the lengths of properties that have them
 *
 * Notice that the `reg` and `interrupts` properties have special
 * macros, like DT_REG_ADDR() and DT_IRQN(). Prefer those over using
 * DT_PROP(node_id, reg) and DT_PROP(node_id, interrupts) directly
 * unless you have a good reason not to.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     node_1: node-1 {
 *             my-int = <1>;
 *             my-bytes = [02 03];
 *             my-str = "foo";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     #define NODE_1 DT_NODELABEL(node_1)
 *     DT_PROP(NODE_1, my_int)   // 1
 *     DT_PROP(NODE_1, my_bytes) // {0x02, 0x03}
 *     DT_PROP(NODE_1, my_str)   // "foo"
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @return a representation of the property's value
 */
#define DT_PROP(node_id, prop) DT_CAT3(node_id, _P_, prop)

/**
 * @brief Get a property's logical length
 *
 * Here, "length" is a number of elements, which may differ from the
 * property's size in bytes.
 *
 * The return value depends on the property's type:
 *
 * - for types array, phandles, string-array, and uint8-array, this
 *   expands to the number of elements in the array
 * - for type phandle-array, this expands to the number of
 *   phandle and specifier blocks in the property
 * - for typephandle, this expands to 1 (so a phandle is treated as
 *   a degenerate phandles with length 1)
 * - for type string, this expands to the length of the string literal
 *   (as in `strlen(DT_PROP(node_id, prop))`, not including the
 *   trailing NUL)
 *
 * Notice that some special properties, like `ranges`, `reg`, `interrupts`,
 * and `dma-ranges` have variable length entry format depending on context
 * when viewed as raw arrays of numbers in DTS. `DT_PROP_LEN()` on these
 * properties returns the number of entries (such as register blocks for
 * `reg`, or interrupt specifiers for `interrupts`) in the property, *not*
 * the total number of cells in the property's raw DTS representation.
 * Whenever possible, prefer specialized macros like DT_NUM_REGS() or
 * DT_NUM_IRQS() when working with these properties.
 *
 * The behavior of this macro is undefined for properties of other
 * types.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @return the property's length
 */
#define DT_PROP_LEN(node_id, prop) DT_CAT4(node_id, _P_, prop, _LEN)

/**
 * @brief Like DT_PROP_LEN(), but with a fallback to `default_value`
 *
 * If the property is defined (as determined by DT_NODE_HAS_PROP()),
 * this expands to DT_PROP_LEN(node_id, prop). The `default_value`
 * parameter is not expanded in this case.
 *
 * Otherwise, this expands to `default_value`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param default_value a fallback value to expand to
 * @return the property's length or the given default value
 */
#define DT_PROP_LEN_OR(node_id, prop, default_value) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_NODE_HAS_PROP(node_id, prop), \
		    (DT_PROP_LEN(node_id, prop)), (default_value))

/**
 * @brief Is index `idx` valid for an array type property?
 *
 * If this returns 1, then DT_PROP_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx) or
 * DT_PHA_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx, ...) are valid at preprocessor
 * time. If it returns 0, it is an error to use those macros with that
 * index.
 *
 * These return values may be used in `#if` conditionals.
 *
 * Notice that the `reg` and `interrupts` properties have special
 * macros, like DT_REG_HAS_IDX() and DT_IRQ_HAS_IDX(). Prefer those
 * over using `DT_PROP_HAS_IDX(node_id, reg, ...)` and
 * `DT_PROP_HAS_IDX(node_id, interrupts, ...)` directly unless you
 * have a good reason not to.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop a property whose logical length can be queried with
 *             DT_PROP_LEN()
 * @param idx index to check
 * @returnAn expression which evaluates to 1 if `idx` is a valid index
 *         into the given property, and 0 otherwise.
 */
#define DT_PROP_HAS_IDX(node_id, prop, idx) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT6(node_id, _P_, prop, _IDX_, idx, _EXISTS))

/**
 * @brief Get the value at index `idx` in an array type property
 *
 *Wait: before using this macro, check if your property has a
 * specialized API that works better.
 *
 * For example, you should use DT_PHA_BY_IDX() for phandle-array
 * properties, DT_REG_ADDR_BY_IDX() and friends for `reg` properties,
 * and DT_IRQ_BY_IDX() for `interrupts` properties.
 *
 * For properties whose bindings have the following types, this macro
 * expands to:
 *
 * - array, uint8-array: the integer literal at index `idx`
 * - string-array: the string literal at index `idx`
 * - phandles: a node identifier for the node at index `idx`
 * - phandle-array: a node identifier for the node with the phandle at
 *   index `idx` (Wait: do you want DT_PHA_BY_IDX() instead?)
 * - string: the character literal at index `idx` in the string
 *
 * Indices are zero-based.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param idx the index to get
 * @return a representation of the idx-th element of the property
 */
#define DT_PROP_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx) \
	DT_CAT5(node_id, _P_, prop, _IDX_, idx)

/**
 * @brief Like DT_PROP(), but with a fallback to `default_value`
 *
 * If the value exists, this expands to DT_PROP(node_id, prop).
 * The `default_value` parameter is not expanded in this case.
 *
 * Otherwise, this expands to `default_value`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param default_value a fallback value to expand to
 * @return the property's value or `default_value`
 */
#define DT_PROP_OR(node_id, prop, default_value) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_NODE_HAS_PROP(node_id, prop), \
		    (DT_PROP(node_id, prop)), (default_value))

/**
 * @brief Equivalent to DT_PROP(node_id, prop), but converts the
 *        property's string value to a token.
 *
 * This macro may only be used for properties with string type.
 *
 * It converts the property's value to a token by replacing every
 * non-alphanumeric character with an underscore. It retains the case
 * of each letter in the string; thus, `"foo_BAR"` becomes `foo_BAR`,
 * and `"123.456"` becomes `123_456`.
 *
 * The result is a valid C identifier on its own if the string starts
 * with an alphabetical character (or underscore), and can always be
 * pasted onto another valid identifier carefully.
 *
 * Notice that if the property's binding has an `enum:` specifier,
 * you may want DT_ENUM_IDX() instead.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n1: node-1 {
 *             prop = "foo";
 *     };
 *     n2: node-2 {
 *             prop = "FOO";
 *     };
 *     n3: node-3 {
 *             prop = "123 foo";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_STRING_TOKEN(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop) // foo
 *     DT_STRING_TOKEN(DT_NODELABEL(n2), prop) // FOO
 *     DT_STRING_TOKEN(DT_NODELABEL(n3), prop) // 123_foo
 * @endcode
 *
 * Notice how:
 *
 * - Unlike C identifiers, the property values may begin with a
 *   number. It's the user's responsibility not to use the
 *   resulting token as the name of a C identifier by itself.
 *   (Pasting it as a suffix onto a valid identifier, like
 *   `UTIL_CAT(PREFIX_, DT_STRING_TOKEN(node_id, prop))`, is fine.)
 * - The `n1` property `"foo"` is converted to `foo` in lowercase,
 *   while `n2` property `"FOO"` is converted to `FOO` in uppercase.
 * - Whitespace in the `n3` property `"123 foo"` is converted to
 *   an underscore in `123_foo`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @return the value of `prop` as a token, i.e. without any quotes
 *         and with special characters converted to underscores
 */
#define DT_STRING_TOKEN(node_id, prop) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _P_, prop, _STRING_TOKEN)

/**
 * @brief Like DT_STRING_TOKEN(), but with a fallback to `default_value`
 *
 * If the value exists, this expands to DT_STRING_TOKEN(node_id, prop).
 * The `default_value` parameter is not expanded in this case.
 *
 * Otherwise, this expands to `default_value`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param default_value a fallback value to expand to
 * @return the property's value as a token, or `default_value`
 */
#define DT_STRING_TOKEN_OR(node_id, prop, default_value) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_NODE_HAS_PROP(node_id, prop), \
		    (DT_STRING_TOKEN(node_id, prop)), (default_value))

/**
 * @brief Like DT_STRING_TOKEN(), but Uppercased
 *
 * This macro may only be used for properties with string type.
 *
 * It converts the property's value to an uppercase token by replacing
 * every non-alphanumeric character with an underscore, and
 * capitalizing every letter. Thus, `"foo_bar"` becomes `FOO_BAR`, and
 * `"123.456"` becomes `123_456`.
 *
 *Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n1: node-1 {
 *             prop = "foo";
 *     };
 *     n2: node-2 {
 *             prop = "123 Foo";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop) // FOO
 *     DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN(DT_NODELABEL(n2), prop) // 123_FOO
 * @endcode
 *
 * For more details and caveats, see DT_STRING_TOKEN().
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @return the value of `prop` as an uppercase token, i.e. without
 *         any quotes, with special characters converted to underscores,
 *         and with letters capitalized.
 */
#define DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN(node_id, prop) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _P_, prop, _STRING_UPPER_TOKEN)

/**
 * @brief Like DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN(), but with a fallback to `default_value`
 *
 * If the value exists, this expands to DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN(node_id, prop).
 * The `default_value` parameter is not expanded in this case.
 *
 * Otherwise, this expands to `default_value`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param default_value a fallback value to expand to
 * @return the property's value as an uppercase token, or `default_value`
 */
#define DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN_OR(node_id, prop, default_value) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_NODE_HAS_PROP(node_id, prop), \
		    (DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN(node_id, prop)), (default_value))

/**
 * @brief Equivalent to DT_PROP(node_id, prop), butelapsed as a string
 *        without quotes.
 *
 * This macro may only be used for properties with string type.
 *
 * It expands to the property's string contents as a sequence of C
 * tokens, without any double quotes (`"`) around it.
 *
 * Take care when using this macro: since the string contents can be
 * arbitrary, it can easily produce invalid C code.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n1: node-1 {
 *             prop = "1.0f";
 *     };
 *     n2: node-2 {
 *             prop = "0.01";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     float f = DT_STRING_UNQUOTED(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop); // float f = 1.0f;
 *     double d = DT_STRING_UNQUOTED(DT_NODELABEL(n2), prop); // double d = 0.01;
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @return the property's string value as a literal sequence of tokens,
 *         with no quotes
 */
#define DT_STRING_UNQUOTED(node_id, prop) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _P_, prop, _STRING_UNQUOTED)

/**
 * @brief Like DT_STRING_UNQUOTED(), but with a fallback to `default_value`
 *
 * If the value exists, this expands to DT_STRING_UNQUOTED(node_id, prop).
 * The `default_value` parameter is not expanded in this case.
 *
 * Otherwise, this expands to `default_value`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param default_value a fallback value to expand to
 * @return the property's value as a sequence of tokens, with no quotes,
 *         or `default_value`
 */
#define DT_STRING_UNQUOTED_OR(node_id, prop, default_value) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_NODE_HAS_PROP(node_id, prop), \
		    (DT_STRING_UNQUOTED(node_id, prop)), (default_value))

/**
 * @brief Equivalent to DT_PROP_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx), but converts
 *        the string value at index `idx` to a token.
 *
 * This macro may only be used for properties with string-array type.
 *
 * It converts the idx-th element's string value to a token in the same
 * way that DT_STRING_TOKEN() converts a single string property.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n1: node-1 {
 *             prop = "f1", "F2", "123 foo";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_STRING_TOKEN_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop, 0) // f1
 *     DT_STRING_TOKEN_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop, 1) // F2
 *     DT_STRING_TOKEN_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop, 2) // 123_foo
 * @endcode
 *
 * For more details, see DT_STRING_TOKEN().
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param idx the index to get
 * @return the element of `prop` at index `idx` as a token
 */
#define DT_STRING_TOKEN_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx) \
	DT_CAT6(node_id, _P_, prop, _IDX_, idx, _STRING_TOKEN)

/**
 * @brief Like DT_STRING_TOKEN_BY_IDX(), but uppercased
 *
 * This macro may only be used for properties with string-array type.
 *
 * It converts the idx-th element's string value to an uppercase token
 * in the same way that DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN() converts a single
 * string property.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n1: node-1 {
 *             prop = "f1", "F2", "123 foo";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop, 0) // F1
 *     DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop, 1) // F2
 *     DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop, 2) // 123_FOO
 * @endcode
 *
 * For more details, see DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN().
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param idx the index to get
 * @return the element of `prop` at index `idx` as an uppercase token
 */
#define DT_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx) \
	DT_CAT6(node_id, _P_, prop, _IDX_, idx, _STRING_UPPER_TOKEN)

/**
 * @brief Equivalent to DT_PROP_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx), but expands
 *        the string value at index `idx` without quotes.
 *
 * This macro may only be used for properties with string-array type.
 *
 * It expands the idx-th element's string value as a sequence of tokens,
 * with no quotes around it, in the same way that DT_STRING_UNQUOTED()
 * expands a single string property.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n1: node-1 {
 *             prop = "1.0f", "0.01";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     float f = DT_STRING_UNQUOTED_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop, 0); // float f = 1.0f;
 *     double d = DT_STRING_UNQUOTED_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(n1), prop, 1); // double d = 0.01;
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param idx the index to get
 * @return the element of `prop` at index `idx` as a sequence of tokens,
 *         with no quotes
 */
#define DT_STRING_UNQUOTED_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx) \
	DT_CAT6(node_id, _P_, prop, _IDX_, idx, _STRING_UNQUOTED)

/*
 * Helpers for playful properties
 */

/**
 * @brief Get a property value's index into its enumeration values
 *
 * The return value start at zero.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     usb1: usb@12340000 {
 *             maximum-speed = "full-speed";
 *     };
 *     usb2: usb@12341000 {
 *             maximum-speed = "super-speed";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example binding fragment:
 *
 * @code{.yaml}
 *     properties:
 *       maximum-speed:
 *         type: string
 *         enum:
 *            - "low-speed"
 *            - "full-speed"
 *            - "high-speed"
 *            - "super-speed"
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_ENUM_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(usb1), maximum_speed) // 1
 *     DT_ENUM_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(usb2), maximum_speed) // 3
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @return zero-based index of the property's value in its enum: list
 */
#define DT_ENUM_IDX(node_id, prop) DT_CAT4(node_id, _P_, prop, _ENUM_IDX)

/**
 * @brief Get a property value's index into its enumeration values at index `idx`
 *
 * The return values start at zero.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     node1: node@12340000 {
 *             list- items = "zero", "two", "one";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example binding fragment:
 *
 * @code{.yaml}
 *     properties:
 *       list-items:
 *         type: string-array
 *         enum:
 *            - "zero"
 *            - "one"
 *            - "two"
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_ENUM_IDX_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(node1), list_items, 0) // 0
 *     DT_ENUM_IDX_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(node1), list_items, 1) // 2
 *     DT_ENUM_IDX_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(node1), list_items, 2) // 1
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param idx index into the property array to get the enum index of
 * @return zero-based index of the property's idx-th element in its enum: list
 */
#define DT_ENUM_IDX_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx) \
	DT_CAT6(node_id, _P_, prop, _IDX_, idx, _ENUM_IDX)

/**
 * @brief Like DT_ENUM_IDX(), but with a fallback to a default enum index
 *
 * If the value exists, this expands to DT_ENUM_IDX(node_id, prop).
 *
 * Otherwise, this expands to the default value provided.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param default_idx_value a fallback index value to expand to
 * @return zero-based index of the property's value in its enum: list if
 *         present, `default_idx_value` otherwise
 */
#define DT_ENUM_IDX_OR(node_id, prop, default_idx_value) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_NODE_HAS_PROP(node_id, prop), \
		    (DT_ENUM_IDX(node_id, prop)), (default_idx_value))

/**
 * @brief Like DT_ENUM_IDX_BY_IDX(), but with a fallback to a default enum index
 *
 * If the value exists at the given index, this expands to
 * DT_ENUM_IDX_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx).
 *
 * Otherwise, this expands to the default value provided.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param idx index into the property array to get the enum index of
 * @param default_idx_value a fallback index value to expand to
 * @return zero-based index of the property's idx-th element in its enum: list if
 *         present, `default_idx_value` otherwise
 */
#define DT_ENUM_IDX_BY_IDX_OR(node_id, prop, idx, default_idx_value) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_PROP_HAS_IDX(node_id, prop, idx), \
		    (DT_ENUM_IDX_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx)), (default_idx_value))

/**
 * @brief Does a node enumeration property have a given value?
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param val lowercase-and-underscores enumeration value
 * @return 1 if the node has the property `prop` with the value `val`,
 *         0 otherwise.
 */
#define DT_ENUM_HAS_VALUE(node_id, prop, val) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT6(node_id, _P_, prop, _ENUM_VAL_, val, _EXISTS))

/**
 * @brief Does a node array enumeration property have a given value at index `idx`?
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param idx index into the property array to check
 * @param val lowercase-and-underscores enumeration value
 * @return 1 if the node has the property `prop` with the value `val` at index `idx`,

 */
#define DT_ENUM_HAS_VALUE_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx, val) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT8(node_id, _P_, prop, _IDX_, idx, _ENUM_VAL_, val, _EXISTS))

/*
 * Phandle properties
 */

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for a phandle in a property.
 *
 * When a node's value at a logical index contains a phandle, this
 * macro returns a node identifier for the node with that phandle.
 *
 * Therefore, this macro can be used for properties with type
 * `phandle`, `phandles`, and `phandle-array`. However, Notice that an
 * ordinary `DT_PROP(node_id, prop)` also expands to a node identifier
 * for a `phandle` property, and it is simpler to use.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n1: node-1 {
 *             phandle-array-prop = <&n2 1 2>, <&n3 3 4>;
 *     };
 *
 *     n2: node-2 { ... };
 *     n3: node-3 { ... };
 * @endcode
 *
 *Above, `phandle-array-prop` has two elements:
 *
 * - index 0 has phandle `&n2`, and specifier `<1 2>`
 * - index 1 has phandle `&n3`, and specifier `<3 4>`
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     #define N1 DT_NODELABEL(n1)
 *
 *     DT_PHANDLE_BY_IDX(N1, phandle_array_prop, 0) // node identifier for node-2
 *     DT_PHANDLE_BY_IDX(N1, phandle_array_prop, 1) // node identifier for node-3
 * @endcode
 *
 * Wait: for `phandle-array`, do you want a specifier value instead?
 * If so, check DT_PHA_BY_IDX() and its related macros.
 *
 * Behavior is analogous for `phandles`, where each array element is
 * just a phandle, and `phandle`, where the only valid `idx` is 0.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param idx logical index into `prop`
 * @return node identifier for the node with the phandle at that index
 */
#define DT_PHANDLE_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx) \
	DT_CAT6(node_id, _P_, prop, _IDX_, idx, _PH)

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for a phandle in a property by name
 *
 * This is a convenience around DT_PHANDLE_BY_IDX() when the
 * phandle-array has an accompanying `*-names` property which names
 * each element in the array.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n1: node-1 {
 *             io-channels = <&adc1 10>, <&adc2 20>;
 *             io-channel-names = "SENSOR", "BANDGAP";
 *     };
 *
 *     adc1: adc@12340000 { ... };
 *     adc2: adc@12341000 { ... };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     #define N1 DT_NODELABEL(n1)
 *
 *     DT_PHANDLE_BY_NAME(N1, io_channels, sensor)  // node identifier for adc1
 *     DT_PHANDLE_BY_NAME(N1, io_channels, bandgap) // node identifier for adc2
 * @endcode
 *
 * Notice how `"SENSOR"` and `"BANDGAP"` in the devicetree must be
 * lowercased when passed to DT_PHANDLE_BY_NAME(). Any non-alphanumeric
 * characters are converted to underscores as usual.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param pha lowercase-and-underscores phandle-array property name
 * @param name lowercase-and-underscores name of an element in `pha`
 * @return node identifier for the phandle at that element
 */
#define DT_PHANDLE_BY_NAME(node_id, pha, name) \
	DT_CAT6(node_id, _P_, pha, _NAME_, name, _PH)

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for a phandle property's value
 *
 * This is equivalent to DT_PHANDLE_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, 0). Its primary
 * use is as a shorthand for `phandle-array` properties with a single
 * element,though it also works for `phandle` and `phandles`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @return a node identifier for the phandle at index 0 in `prop`
 */
#define DT_PHANDLE(node_id, prop) DT_PHANDLE_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, 0)

/*
 * Helpers for phandle-array properties
 */

/**
 * @brief Get a phandle-array specifier cell value at an index
 *
 * It may help to read the argument names as: "node_id's phandle-array
 * at index takes cell". That is, the return value is the value of
 * cell `cell` within the specifier at index `idx` inside the
 * phandle-array property `pha` of `node_id`.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n1: node-1 {
 *             gpios = <&gpioa 10 GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>,
 *                     <&gpiob 20 GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>;
 *     };
 *
 *     gpioa: gpio@12340000 {
 *             #gpio-cells = <2>;
 *     };
 *
 *     gpiob: gpio@12341000 {
 *             #gpio-cells = <2>;
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example binding fragment for the `gpioa` and `gpiob` nodes:
 *
 * @code{.yaml}
 *     gpio-cells:
 *       - pin
 *       - flags
 * @endcode
 *
 * Above, `gpios` has two elements:
 *
 * - index 0 has specifier `<10 GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>`, so its `pin` cell is 10,
 *   and its `flags` cell is `GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH`
 * - index 1 has specifier `<20 GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW>`, so its `pin` cell is 20,
 *   and its `flags` cell is `GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW`

 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     #define N1 DT_NODELABEL(n1)
 *
 *     DT_PHA_BY_IDX(N1, gpios, 0, pin)   // 10
 *     DT_PHA_BY_IDX(N1, gpios, 1, flags) // GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW
 * @endcode

 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param pha lowercase-and-underscores phandle-array property name
 * @param idx logical index into the property `pha`
 * @param cell lowercase-and-underscores cell name within the specifier
 *             at `pha` index `idx`
 * @return the value of that cell inside the specifier at index `idx`

	DT_CAT7(node_id, _P_, pha, _IDX_, idx, _VAL_, cell)

/**
 * @brief Like DT_PHA_BY_IDX(), but with a fallback to `default_value`.

 * @param node_id node identifier

 * @param default_value a fallback value to expand to

#define DT_PHA_BY_IDX_OR(node_id, pha, idx, cell, default_value) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_PHA_HAS_CELL_AT_IDX(node_id, pha, idx, cell), \

/**
 * @brief Is the property `ranges` present and non-empty?
 *
 * Every `ranges` property is either empty (e.g. `ranges;`), meaning
 * 1:1 address translation applies, or is a list of (child-bus-address,
 * parent-bus-address, length) tuples.
 *
 * This macro returns 1 if the node has a `ranges` property which is
 * not empty, and 0 otherwise (i.e. if the node has an empty `ranges;`
 * property, or has no `ranges` property at all).
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return 1 if `ranges` is present and non-empty, 0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_NUM_RANGES(node_id) DT_CAT(node_id, _RANGES_NUM)

/**
 * @brief Is `idx` a valid `ranges` tuple index for the node?
 *
 * If this returns 1, then `idx` is a valid index into the node's
 * `ranges` property, and macros like `DT_RANGES_CHILD_BUS_ADDRESS_BY_IDX(node_id, idx)`
 * are safe to use. If it returns 0, then `idx` is out of bounds (or
 * the node has no `ranges` tuples).
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx index to check
 * @return 1 if `idx` is a valid `ranges` index, 0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_RANGES_HAS_IDX(node_id, idx) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT4(node_id, _RANGES_IDX_, idx, _EXISTS))

/**
 * @brief Does the `ranges` tuple at `idx` have a child bus flags cell?
 *
 * In PCI and PCIe bus bindings, the child bus address is a 3-cell
 * structure whose first cell contains flags (like prefetchable,
 * space code, etc.), rather than just a flat address.
 *
 * This macro returns 1 if the `ranges` tuple at `idx` has such a
 * flags cell, and 0 otherwise.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx logical index into `ranges`
 * @return 1 if the tuple at `idx` has child bus flags, 0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_RANGES_HAS_CHILD_BUS_FLAGS_BY_IDX(node_id, idx) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT4(node_id, _RANGES_IDX_, idx, _VAL_CHILD_BUS_FLAGS_EXISTS))

/**
 * @brief Get the `ranges` tuple's child bus flags at index
 *
 * When DT_RANGES_HAS_CHILD_BUS_FLAGS_BY_IDX(node_id, idx) is true, this
 * returns the value of the child bus flags cell at `idx`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx logical index into `ranges`
 * @return the child bus flags cell at index `idx`
 */
#define DT_RANGES_CHILD_BUS_FLAGS_BY_IDX(node_id, idx) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _RANGES_IDX_, idx, _VAL_CHILD_BUS_FLAGS)

/**
 * @brief Get the `ranges` tuple's child bus address at index
 *
 * Notice that for PCI/PCIe busses (where DT_RANGES_HAS_CHILD_BUS_FLAGS_BY_IDX()
 * is true), this returns the 64-bit address formed from the remaining
 * two cells, excluding the flags cell.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx logical index into `ranges`
 * @return the child bus address at index `idx`
 */
#define DT_RANGES_CHILD_BUS_ADDRESS_BY_IDX(node_id, idx) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _RANGES_IDX_, idx, _VAL_CHILD_BUS_ADDRESS)

/**
 * @brief Get the `ranges` tuple's parent bus address at index
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx logical index into `ranges`
 * @return the parent bus address at index `idx`
 */
#define DT_RANGES_PARENT_BUS_ADDRESS_BY_IDX(node_id, idx) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _RANGES_IDX_, idx, _VAL_PARENT_BUS_ADDRESS)

/**
 * @brief Get the `ranges` tuple's length at index
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx logical index into `ranges`
 * @return the length at index `idx`
 */
#define DT_RANGES_LENGTH_BY_IDX(node_id, idx) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _RANGES_IDX_, idx, _VAL_LENGTH)

/**
 * @brief Call `fn` on all tuples in the node's `ranges` property
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take two arguments: `node_id` and `idx`. It is
 * invoked once for each tuple in the `ranges` property, with `idx`
 * set to 0, 1, ..., DT_NUM_RANGES(node_id) - 1.
 *
 * If the node has no `ranges` property (or an empty `ranges;` property),
 * this expands to nothing.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param fn macro to invoke on each tuple
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_RANGE(node_id, fn) \
	DT_CAT(node_id, _FOREACH_RANGE)(fn)

/**
 * @brief Call `fn` on all tuples in the node's `ranges` property
 *        with extra arguments
 *
 * Like DT_FOREACH_RANGE(), but passes any extra arguments `...` to
 * `fn` after `node_id` and `idx`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param fn macro to invoke on each tuple
 * @param ... extra arguments to pass to `fn`
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_RANGE_VARGS(node_id, fn, ...) \
	DT_CAT(node_id, _FOREACH_RANGE_VARGS)(fn, __VA_ARGS__)

 * of the interrupt controller that the node's interrupt is connected
 * to (1 for a 1st-level aggregator connected directly to the CPU, 2
 * for a 2nd-level aggregator chained to a 1st-level one, etc.), *not*
 * the priority or trigger level (active-high vs active-low) of the
 * interrupt signal.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx interrupt specifier index
 * @return interrupt hierarchy level at index `idx`
 */
#define DT_IRQ_LEVEL_BY_IDX(node_id, idx) DT_CAT4(node_id, _IRQ_IDX_, idx, _VAL_LEVEL)

/**
 * @brief Equivalent to DT_IRQ_LEVEL_BY_IDX(node_id, 0)
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return interrupt hierarchy level at index 0
 */
#define DT_IRQ_LEVEL(node_id) DT_IRQ_LEVEL_BY_IDX(node_id, 0)

/**
 * @brief Is `idx` a valid interrupt index for the node?
 *
 * If this returns 1, then DT_IRQ_BY_IDX(node_id, idx, cell) may be
 * valid at preprocessor time (depending on whether `cell` exists).
 * If it returns 0, it is an error to use DT_IRQ_BY_IDX() with this
 * index.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx index to check
 * @return 1 if the `idx` is valid for the node's interrupts, 0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_IRQ_HAS_IDX(node_id, idx) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT4(node_id, _IRQ_IDX_, idx, _EXISTS))

/**
 * @brief Does an interrupt specifier have a named cell at an index?
 *
 * If this returns 1, then DT_IRQ_BY_IDX(node_id, idx, cell) is valid
 * at preprocessor time. If it returns 0, it is an error to use
 * DT_IRQ_BY_IDX() with the same arguments.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx index to check
 * @param cell lowercase-and-underscores cell name whose existence to check
 * @return 1 if the named cell exists in the interrupt specifier at index `idx`,
 *         0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_IRQ_HAS_CELL_AT_IDX(node_id, idx, cell) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT6(node_id, _IRQ_IDX_, idx, _VAL_, cell, _EXISTS))

/**
 * @brief Equivalent to DT_IRQ_HAS_CELL_AT_IDX(node_id, 0, cell)
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param cell lowercase-and-underscores cell name whose existence to check
 * @return 1 if the named cell exists in the interrupt specifier at index 0,
 *         0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_IRQ_HAS_CELL(node_id, cell) DT_IRQ_HAS_CELL_AT_IDX(node_id, 0, cell)

/**
 * @brief Does a node's interrupts property have a named specifier?
 *
 * If this returns 1, then DT_IRQ_BY_NAME(node_id, name, cell) may be
 * valid at preprocessor time (depending on whether `cell` exists).
 * If it returns 0, it is an error to use DT_IRQ_BY_NAME() with this
 * name.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param name lowercase-and-underscores interrupt specifier name
 * @return 1 if `name` is a valid name for an interrupt specifier, 0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_IRQ_HAS_NAME(node_id, name) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT4(node_id, _IRQ_NAME_, name, _VAL_irq_EXISTS))

/**
 * @brief Get a value within an interrupt specifier at an index
 *
 * It might help to read the argument names as "node_id's interrupt at
 * index has cell".
 *
 * This can be used to get information about an individual interrupt
 * when a device generates more than one. Zero-based indices are used.
 *
 * Each interrupt source for a node has a corresponding specifier
 * whose structure is determined by the interrupt controller node's
 * `#interrupt-cells` property and binding. In Zephyr's devicetree
 * bindings, each cell in `#interrupt-cells` is given a name, just
 * like with phandle-arrays. You can use this macro to look up cell
 * values by cell name and interrupt index.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx logical index into the interrupt specifier array
 * @param cell cell name lookup within the specifier at index `idx`
 * @return the value of that cell inside the specifier at index `idx`
 */
#define DT_IRQ_BY_IDX(node_id, idx, cell) \
	DT_CAT5(node_id, _IRQ_IDX_, idx, _VAL_, cell)

/**
 * @brief Get a value within an interrupt specifier by name
 *
 * This is like DT_IRQ_BY_IDX(), except it identifies the interrupt
 * entry by its name in the node's `interrupt-names` property.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param name lowercase-and-underscores interrupt specifier name
 * @param cell cell name lookup within the named specifier
 * @return the value of that cell inside the named specifier
 */
#define DT_IRQ_BY_NAME(node_id, name, cell) \
	DT_CAT5(node_id, _IRQ_NAME_, name, _VAL_, cell)

/**
 * @brief Get a value within a node's (only) interrupt specifier
 *
 * Equivalent to DT_IRQ_BY_IDX(node_id, 0, cell).
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param cell cell name within the specifier
 * @return the cell value at index 0
 */
#define DT_IRQ(node_id, cell) DT_IRQ_BY_IDX(node_id, 0, cell)

/**
 * @brief Get the interrupt controller node for an interrupt at an index
 *
 * This returns a node identifier for the interrupt controller that
 * processes the interrupt at index `idx` for `node_id`.
 *
 * Wait: this resolves both `interrupt-parent` and `interrupts-extended`
 * automatically.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     / {
 *             intc1: interrupt-controller@1000 {
 *                     interrupt-controller;
 *                     #interrupt-cells = <1>;
 *             };
 *
 *             intc2: interrupt-controller@2000 {
 *                     interrupt-controller;
 *                     #interrupt-cells = <1>;
 *             };
 *
 *             soc {
 *                     interrupt-parent = <&intc1>;
 *
 *                     dev1: device@1 {
 *                             interrupts = <10>;
 *                     };
 *
 *                     dev2: device@2 {
 *                             interrupts-extended = <&intc1 20>, <&intc2 30>;
 *                     };
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_IRQ_INTC_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(dev1), 0) // node identifier for intc1
 *     DT_IRQ_INTC_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(dev2), 0) // node identifier for intc1
 *     DT_IRQ_INTC_BY_IDX(DT_NODELABEL(dev2), 1) // node identifier for intc2
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx interrupt specifier index
 * @return node identifier for the interrupt controller for index `idx`
 */
#define DT_IRQ_INTC_BY_IDX(node_id, idx) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _IRQ_IDX_, idx, _CONTROLLER)

/**
 * @brief Get the interrupt controller node for a named interrupt
 *
 * This is like DT_IRQ_INTC_BY_IDX(), except it looks up the interrupt
 * by name using `interrupt-names`.
 *
 *Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     / {
 *             intc1: interrupt-controller@1000 {
 *                     interrupt-controller;
 *                     #interrupt-cells = <1>;
 *             };
 *
 *             intc2: interrupt-controller@2000 {
 *                     interrupt-controller;
 *                     #interrupt-cells = <1>;
 *             };
 *
 *             dev: device@0 {
 *                     interrupts-extended = <&intc1 20>, <&intc2 30>;
 *                     interrupt-names = "rx", "tx";
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_IRQ_INTC_BY_NAME(DT_NODELABEL(dev), rx) // node identifier for intc1
 *     DT_IRQ_INTC_BY_NAME(DT_NODELABEL(dev), tx) // node identifier for intc2
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param name lowercase-and-underscores interrupt specifier name
 * @return node identifier for the interrupt controller for `name`
 */
#define DT_IRQ_INTC_BY_NAME(node_id, name) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _IRQ_NAME_, name, _CONTROLLER)

/**
 * @brief Get the interrupt controller node for a node's (only) interrupt
 *
 * Equivalent to DT_IRQ_INTC_BY_IDX(node_id, 0).
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return node identifier for the node's only interrupt's controller
 */
#define DT_IRQ_INTC(node_id) DT_IRQ_INTC_BY_IDX(node_id, 0)

/**
 * @brief Get a node's (only) irq number
 *
 * Equivalent to DT_IRQ(node_id, irq), except when multi-level
 * interrupts are enabled, in which case it returns the encoded
 * multi-level IRQ number recognized by Zephyr's interrupt subsystem.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return the interrupt number for the node's only interrupt
 */
#define DT_IRQN(node_id) DT_IRQN_BY_IDX(node_id, 0)

/**
 * @brief Get a node's irq number at an index
 *
 * Equivalent to DT_IRQ_BY_IDX(node_id, idx, irq) when multi-level
 * interrupts are not enabled.
 *
 * When `CONFIG_MULTI_LEVEL_INTERRUPTS` is enabled, this returns the
 * encoded multi-level IRQ number recognized by Zephyr's interrupt
 * subsystem for the interrupt at `idx`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param idx interrupt specifier index
 * @return the interrupt number at index `idx`
 */
#define DT_IRQN_BY_IDX(node_id, idx) \
	COND_CODE_1(IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MULTI_LEVEL_INTERRUPTS), \
		    (DT_CAT4(node_id, _IRQ_IDX_, idx, _VAL_irq)), \
		    (DT_IRQ_BY_IDX(node_id, idx, irq)))

/**
 * @brief Get a node's irq number by name
 *
 * Equivalent to DT_IRQ_BY_NAME(node_id, name, irq) when multi-level
 * interrupts are not enabled.
 *
 * When `CONFIG_MULTI_LEVEL_INTERRUPTS` is enabled, this returns the
 * encoded multi-level IRQ number recognized by Zephyr's interrupt
 * subsystem for the interrupt named `name`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param name lowercase-and-underscores interrupt specifier name
 * @return the interrupt number for `name`
 */
#define DT_IRQN_BY_NAME(node_id, name) \
	COND_CODE_1(IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_MULTI_LEVEL_INTERRUPTS), \
		    (DT_CAT4(node_id, _IRQ_NAME_, name, _VAL_irq)), \
		    (DT_IRQ_BY_NAME(node_id, name, irq)))

/**
 * @cond INTERNAL_HIDDEN
 */

/* Helper macros for DT_IRQN_BY_IDX; do not use directly */
#define DT_MULTI_LEVEL_IRQN_INTERNAL(node_id, idx) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _IRQ_IDX_, idx, _VAL_irq_ENC)

/**
 * @endcond
 */

/**
 * @brief Get a node identifier for a `/chosen` node property

 * This is only valid to call if `DT_HAS_CHOSEN(prop)` is 1.
 *
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name for
 *             the `/chosen` node
 * @return a node identifier for the chosen node property
 */
#define DT_CHOSEN(prop) DT_CAT(DT_N_CHOSEN_, prop)

/**
 * @brief Test if the devicetree has a `/chosen` node
 *
 * The argument must use lowercase letters, with non-alphanumeric
 * characters converted to underscores.
 *
 * Lookups for `/chosen` properties take place in the root node's
 * `chosen` child.
 *
 * If this returns 1, then `DT_CHOSEN(prop)` is a valid node identifier.
 * If it returns 0, it is an error to use `DT_CHOSEN(prop)`.
 *
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores `/chosen` property name
 * @return 1 if the chosen property exists and refers to a node,
 *         0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_HAS_CHOSEN(prop) IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT3(DT_N_CHOSEN_, prop, _EXISTS))

/**
 * @defgroup devicetree-generic-foreach "For-each" macros
 * @ingroup devicetree
 * @{
 */

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for every child of `node_id`
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take one parameter, which will be the node
 * identifier of a child node of `node_id`.
 *
 * Notice that this iterates over **all** child nodes, including
 * disabled nodes (such as nodes with `status = "disabled"`). To
 * iterate over only enabled child nodes, use
 * DT_FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY() instead.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n: node {
 *             ch1: child-1 {
 *                     label = "foo";
 *             };
 *             ch2: child-2 {
 *                     label = "bar";
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     #define LABEL_AND_COMMA(node_id) DT_PROP(node_id, label),
 *
 *     const char *child_labels[] = {
 *         DT_FOREACH_CHILD(DT_NODELABEL(n), LABEL_AND_COMMA)
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * This expands to:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     const char *child_labels[] = {
 *         "foo", "bar",
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_CHILD(node_id, fn) \
	DT_CAT(node_id, _FOREACH_CHILD)(fn)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for every child of `node_id` with a separator
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take one parameter, which will be the node
 * identifier of a child node of `node_id`.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n: node {
 *             ch1: child-1 {};
 *             ch2: child-2 {};
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     const char *child_names[] = {
 *         DT_FOREACH_CHILD_SEP(DT_NODELABEL(n), DT_NODE_FULL_NAME, (,))
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * This expands to:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     const char *child_names[] = {
 *         "child-1", "child-2"
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 * @param sep Separator (e.g. comma or semicolon). Must be in parentheses;
 *            this is required to enable providing a comma as separator.
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_CHILD_SEP(node_id, fn, sep) \
	DT_CAT(node_id, _FOREACH_CHILD_SEP)(fn, sep)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for every child of `node_id` with multiple arguments
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take one parameter, which will be the node
 * identifier of a child node of `node_id`, followed by the remaining
 * arguments `...` passed to `DT_FOREACH_CHILD_VARGS`.
 *
 * Notice that this iterates over **all** child nodes, including
 * disabled nodes. To iterate over only enabled child nodes, use
 * DT_FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY_VARGS() instead.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 * @param ... variable number of arguments to pass to `fn`
 *
 * @see DT_FOREACH_CHILD
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_CHILD_VARGS(node_id, fn, ...) \
	DT_CAT(node_id, _FOREACH_CHILD_VARGS)(fn, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for every child of `node_id` with a separator and
 *        multiple arguments
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take one parameter, which will be the node
 * identifier of a child node of `node_id`, followed by the remaining
 * arguments `...` passed to `DT_FOREACH_CHILD_SEP_VARGS`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 * @param sep Separator (e.g. comma or semicolon). Must be in parentheses;
 *            this is required to enable providing a comma as separator.
 * @param ... variable number of arguments to pass to `fn`
 *
 * @see DT_FOREACH_CHILD_SEP
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_CHILD_SEP_VARGS(node_id, fn, sep, ...) \
	DT_CAT(node_id, _FOREACH_CHILD_SEP_VARGS)(fn, sep, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for every status `"okay"` child of `node_id`
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take one parameter, which will be the node
 * identifier of a child node of `node_id`. Only child nodes with
 * status `"okay"` (or no `status` property, which defaults to
 * `"okay"`) are visited.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 *
 * @see DT_FOREACH_CHILD
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY(node_id, fn) \
	DT_CAT(node_id, _FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY)(fn)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for every status `"okay"` child of `node_id`
 *        with a separator
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take one parameter, which will be the node
 * identifier of a child node of `node_id`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 * @param sep Separator (e.g. comma or semicolon). Must be in parentheses;
 *            this is required to enable providing a comma as separator.
 *
 * @see DT_FOREACH_CHILD_SEP
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY_SEP(node_id, fn, sep) \
	DT_CAT(node_id, _FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY_SEP)(fn, sep)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for every status `"okay"` child of `node_id`
 *        with multiple arguments
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take one parameter, which will be the node
 * identifier of a child node of `node_id`, followed by the remaining
 * arguments `...` passed to `DT_FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY_VARGS`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 * @param ... variable number of arguments to pass to `fn`
 *
 * @see DT_FOREACH_CHILD_VARGS
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY_VARGS(node_id, fn, ...) \
	DT_CAT(node_id, _FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY_VARGS)(fn, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for every status `"okay"` child of `node_id`
 *        with a separator and multiple arguments
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take one parameter, which will be the node
 * identifier of a child node of `node_id`, followed by the remaining
 * arguments `...` passed to `DT_FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY_SEP_VARGS`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 * @param sep Separator (e.g. comma or semicolon). Must be in parentheses;
 *            this is required to enable providing a comma as separator.
 * @param ... variable number of arguments to pass to `fn`
 *
 * @see DT_FOREACH_CHILD_SEP_VARGS
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY_SEP_VARGS(node_id, fn, sep, ...) \
	DT_CAT(node_id, _FOREACH_CHILD_STATUS_OKAY_SEP_VARGS)(fn, sep, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for each element in the value of property `prop`.
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take three parameters: `fn(node_id, prop, idx)`.
 * `node_id` and `prop` are the same as what is passed to
 * `DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM`, and `idx` is the current index into the
 * array. The `idx` values are integer literals starting from 0.
 *
 * The `prop` parameter must refer to a property which can be passed to
 * DT_PROP_LEN(), with the exception that `ranges`, `reg`, and `interrupts`
 * are not supported even though DT_PROP_LEN() works on them.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n: node {
 *             my-ints = <1 2 3>;
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     #define TIMES_TWO(node_id, prop, idx) \
 * 	       (2 * DT_PROP_BY_IDX(node_id, prop, idx)),
 *
 *     int array[] = {
 *             DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM(DT_NODELABEL(n), my_ints, TIMES_TWO)
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * This expands to:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     int array[] = {
 *             (2 * 1), (2 * 2), (2 * 3),
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * In general, this macro expands to:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     fn(node_id, prop, 0) fn(node_id, prop, 1) [...] fn(node_id, prop, n-1)
 * @endcode
 *
 * where `n` is the number of elements in `prop`, as it would be
 * returned by `DT_PROP_LEN(node_id, prop)`.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM(node_id, prop, fn) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _P_, prop, _FOREACH_PROP_ELEM)(fn)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for each element in the value of property `prop` with
 *        a separator.
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take three parameters: `fn(node_id, prop, idx)`.
 * `node_id` and `prop` are the same as what is passed to
 * `DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_SEP`, and `idx` is the current index into the
 * array. The `idx` values are integer literals starting from 0.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n: node {
 *             my-ints = <1 2 3>;
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     int array[] = {
 *             DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_SEP(DT_NODELABEL(n), my_ints,
 *                                      DT_PROP_BY_IDX, (,))
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * This expands to:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     int array[] = {
 *             1, 2, 3
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * This macro can be used with the same properties as DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM().
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 * @param sep Separator (e.g. comma or semicolon). Must be in parentheses;
 *            this is required to enable providing a comma as separator.
 *
 * @see DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_SEP(node_id, prop, fn, sep) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _P_, prop, _FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_SEP)(fn, sep)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for each element in the value of property `prop` with
 *        multiple arguments.
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take three parameters followed by the variadic
 * arguments: `fn(node_id, prop, idx, ...)`. `node_id` and `prop` are
 * the same as what is passed to `DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_VARGS`, `idx` is
 * the current index into the array, and `...` are the remaining arguments.
 * The `idx` values are integer literals starting from 0.
 *
 * This macro can be used with the same properties as DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM().
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 * @param ... variable number of arguments to pass to `fn`
 *
 * @see DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_VARGS(node_id, prop, fn, ...) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _P_, prop, _FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_VARGS)(fn, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for each element in the value of property `prop` with
 *        separator and multiple arguments.
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take three parameters followed by the variadic
 * arguments: `fn(node_id, prop, idx, ...)`. `node_id` and `prop` are
 * the same as what is passed to `DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_SEP_VARGS`, `idx`
 * is the current index into the array, and `...` are the remaining
 * arguments. The `idx` values are integer literals starting from 0.
 *
 * This macro can be used with the same properties as DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM().
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param prop lowercase-and-underscores property name
 * @param fn macro to invoke
 * @param sep Separator (e.g. comma or semicolon). Must be in parentheses;
 *            this is required to enable providing a comma as separator.
 * @param ... variable number of arguments to pass to `fn`
 *
 * @see DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_SEP
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_SEP_VARGS(node_id, prop, fn, sep, ...) \
	DT_CAT4(node_id, _P_, prop, _FOREACH_PROP_ELEM_SEP_VARGS)( \
		fn, sep, __VA_ARGS__)

/**
 * @brief Call `fn` on all nodes with status `"okay"` (or no status) in
 *         the devicetree that have a given compatible.
 *
 * The macro `fn` must take one argument, which is the node identifier
 * for a node with that `compat` and status `"okay"`.
 *
 * Note that `fn` is only called once for each matching node, even if a
 * node's `compatible` property lists `compat` multiple times.
 *
 * @param compat lowercase-and-underscores devicetree compatible
 * @param fn macro to call for each enabled node with that compatible
 */
#define DT_FOREACH_STATUS_OKAY(compat, fn) \
	COND_CODE_1(DT_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS_OKAY(compat), \
		    (UTIL_CAT(DT_FOREACH_OKAY_, compat)(fn)),	\
		    ())

/**
 * @brief Invokes `fn` for every status `"okay"` node of a compatible
 *        with multiple arguments.
 *
 * This is like DT_FOREACH_STATUS_OKAY() except you can also pass
 * additional arguments `...` to `fn`.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n1: node-1 {
 *             compatible = "vnd,my-device";

/**
 * @brief Does a node identifier refer to a node?
 *
 * Tests whether a node identifier refers to a node which actually
 * exists, i.e. is defined in the devicetree.
 *
 * It doesn't matter whether or not the node has a matching binding, or
 * what the node's status value is. This is purely a check of whether
 * the node exists at all.
 *
 * @param node_id a node identifier
 * @return 1 if the node identifier refers to a node,
 *         0 otherwise.
 */
#define DT_NODE_EXISTS(node_id) IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT(node_id, _EXISTS))

/**
 * @brief Does a node identifier refer to a node with a status?
 *
 * Example uses:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_NODE_HAS_STATUS(DT_PATH(soc, i2c_12340000), okay)
 *     DT_NODE_HAS_STATUS(DT_PATH(soc, i2c_12340000), disabled)
 * @endcode
 *
 * Tests whether:
 *
 * - `node_id` refers to a node which exists, and
 * - the node has a `status` property comparing equal to the string
 *   form of `status` (or has no `status` property if the `status`
 *   parameter is the token `okay`)
 *
 * Notice that when testing for status `okay`, it's usually more
 * readable to use DT_NODE_HAS_STATUS_OKAY(node_id) instead.
 *
 * @param node_id a node identifier
 * @param status a status as a lowercase-and-underscores token, like
 *               `okay` or `disabled`
 * @return 1 if the node has the given status, 0 otherwise.
 */
#define DT_NODE_HAS_STATUS(node_id, status) \
	DT_NODE_HAS_STATUS_INTERNAL(node_id, status)

/**
 * @brief Does a node identifier refer to a node with status `"okay"`?
 *
 * Tests whether:
 *
 * - `node_id` refers to a node which exists, and
 * - the node has a `status` property set to `"okay"` or `"ok"` (or does
 *   not have a `status` property at all)
 *
 * @param node_id a node identifier
 * @return 1 if the node has status `"okay"`, 0 otherwise.
 */
#define DT_NODE_HAS_STATUS_OKAY(node_id) \
	DT_NODE_HAS_STATUS_INTERNAL(node_id, okay)

/**
 * @brief Does the devicetree have at least one status `"okay"` node
 *        with a compatible?
 *
 * If this returns 1, then a node with the given `compat` exists and has
 * status `"okay"` (or no status property).
 *
 * Notice that status `"ok"` is treated as a synonym for `"okay"`.
 * Any other status (including `"disabled"`, `"fail"`, etc.) causes this
 * macro to evaluate to 0 for that node.
 *
 * @param compat lowercase-and-underscores compatible, without quotes
 * @return 1 if at least one status `"okay"` node with compatible
 *         `compat` exists, 0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS_OKAY(compat) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT(DT_COMPAT_HAS_OKAY_, compat))

/**
 * @brief Get the number of status `"okay"` nodes of a given compatible
 *
 * Inspects the devicetree to determine the number of enabled (status
 * `"okay"` or no status) nodes with a given `compatible` property.
 *
 * @param compat lowercase-and-underscores compatible, without quotes
 * @return number of status `"okay"` nodes with compatible `compat`
 */
#define DT_NUM_INST_STATUS_OKAY(compat) \
	UTIL_AND(DT_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS_OKAY(compat),		\
		 UTIL_CAT(DT_N_INST, DT_DASH(compat, NUM_OKAY)))

/**
 * @brief Does a devicetree node match a compatible?
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     n: node {
 *             compatible = "vnd,specific-device", "generic-device";
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usages which evaluate to 1:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_NODE_HAS_COMPAT(DT_NODELABEL(n), vnd_specific_device)
 *     DT_NODE_HAS_COMPAT(DT_NODELABEL(n), generic_device)
 * @endcode
 *
 * This macro only uses the value of the `compatible` property.
 * Whether or not a particular compatible has a Zephyr binding associated
 * with it makes no difference, nor does the node's status.
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param compat lowercase-and-underscores compatible, without quotes
 * @return 1 if the node's `compatible` property contains `compat`,
 *         0 otherwise.
 */
#define DT_NODE_HAS_COMPAT(node_id, compat) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT4(node_id, _COMPAT_MATCHES_, compat, ))

/**
 * @brief Does a devicetree node have both a compatible and a status?
 *
 * This is equivalent to:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     (DT_NODE_HAS_COMPAT(node_id, compat) && \
 *      DT_NODE_HAS_STATUS(node_id, status))
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param compat lowercase-and-underscores compatible, without quotes
 * @param status okay or disabled as a token, not a string
 */
#define DT_NODE_HAS_COMPAT_STATUS(node_id, compat, status) \
	(DT_NODE_HAS_COMPAT(node_id, compat) && \
	 DT_NODE_HAS_STATUS(node_id, status))

/**
 * @brief Does a devicetree node have a property?

 * considers the property to exist. In particular:

 *   boolean property is present** (i.e. true). If a boolean property

#define DT_NODE_HAS_PROP(node_id, prop) \
	IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT4(node_id, _P_, prop, _EXISTS))

/**
 * @briefNode's bus controller
 *
 * Get the node identifier of the node's bus controller. This can be
 * used with @ref DT_ON_BUS() to get a node identifier for the bus
 * controller node.
 *
 * It is an error to use this with a node which has no bus controller.
 *
 * Example devicetree fragment:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     i2c1: i2c@40003000 {
 *             compatible = "vnd,i2c-bus";
 *             ...
 *             sensor: temp-sensor@76 {
 *                     compatible = "vnd,temp-sensor";
 *                     reg = <0x76>;
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Assuming `i2c@40003000`'s binding is an `i2c` bus controller node
 * (i.e., its binding file has `bus: i2c`), and `temp-sensor@76`'s
 * binding has `on-bus: i2c`, the following produces a node identifier
 * for `i2c@40003000`:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_BUS(DT_NODELABEL(sensor))
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @return a node identifier for the node's bus controller
 */
#define DT_BUS(node_id) DT_CAT(node_id, _BUS)

/**
 * @brief Is a node on a bus of a given type?
 *
 * Example devicetree overlay:
 *
 * @code{.dts}
 *     &i2c0 {
 *             temp: temperature-sensor@76 {
 *                     compatible = "vnd,temp-sensor";
 *                     reg = <0x76>;
 *             };
 *     };
 * @endcode
 *
 * Example usage, assuming `i2c0` is an I2C bus controller node, and
 * therefore `temp` is on an `i2c` bus:
 *
 * @code{.c}
 *     DT_ON_BUS(DT_NODELABEL(temp), i2c) // 1
 *     DT_ON_BUS(DT_NODELABEL(temp), spi) // 0
 * @endcode
 *
 * @param node_id node identifier
 * @param bus lowercase-and-underscores bus type as a C token (i.e.
 *            without quotes)
 * @return 1 if the node is on a bus of the given type,
 *         0 otherwise
 */
#define DT_ON_BUS(node_id, bus) IS_ENABLED(DT_CAT3(node_id, _BUS_, bus))
